title: An Artificial Intelligence Model for Predicting Trauma Mortality Among Emergency Department Patients in South Korea: Retrospective Cohort Study
summary: Using Korea’s National Emergency Department Information System data for 6.54 million visits at more than 400 hospitals (2016–2019), an AdaBoost–LightGBM ensemble predicted trauma mortality with AUROC 0.9974 in five-fold cross-validation. It outperformed XGBoost and conventional injury/triage scores in the reported dataset. The authors state that external validation is needed; this does not establish clinical benefit.
ai_technology: AdaBoost–LightGBM ensemble for emergency-department trauma mortality

evidence.tested: Five-fold cross-validation on 6,536,306 Korean emergency visits from more than 400 hospitals (2016–2019) evaluated mortality prediction; the all-feature AdaBoost–LightGBM ensemble reached AUROC 0.9974, compared with XGBoost and conventional injury/triage scores.
evidence.unknown: The authors state that external validation is needed and note potential overfitting. Prediction performance does not show that the public risk calculator improved triage or patient outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: The AdaBoost plus LightGBM ensemble predicted emergency-department mortality from nationwide NEDIS records and identified mortality-associated features; AUROC was 0.9974 in retrospective evaluation.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
